answer: The feature already exists as `matplotlib.__version_info__`. It is a namedtuple modelled after `sys.version_info`, with fields major, minor, micro, releaselevel and serial. It is built by `_parse_to_version_info(__version__)` and exposed lazily through the module `__getattr__`. You can compare it with plain tuples, for example `matplotlib.__version_info__ >= (3, 4, 2)`.

The IndexError came from the RangeSlider polygon having only 4 vertices while set_val wrote to xy[4]. The fix is to build the polygon with 5 vertices, `Polygon(np.zeros([5, 2]), **kwargs)`, so the closing vertex xy[4] exists. `_update_selection_poly` (line 816 and line 821) then writes that vertex and keeps it. The line is not commented out, as the report suggested. I read this from the code and did not run the reproduction.

The fix is already in `Artist.format_cursor_data`. It checks `isinstance(self.norm, BoundaryNorm)` before it would call `norm.inverse`. For a BoundaryNorm it finds the nearest boundary with `argmin` and uses the neighboring boundary spacing as `delta` for the significant digits. Other norms still go through `norm.inverse`.

The bug is in rc_context in matplotlib/lib/matplotlib/__init__.py. It does `orig = dict(rcParams.copy())`. Copying the rcParams reads `rcParams['backend']`, which resolves the auto-backend sentinel. That resolution switches the backend and closes all figures. A later `get_backend()` then clears `Gcf.figs`. The fix is the next line, `del orig['backend']`, which drops the backend from the saved copy so the context doesn't restore it. I read this code but did not run the reproduction.
The fix is already in this checkout. Axes3D.draw in mplot3d/axes3d.py begins with `if not self.get_visible(): return`, so a 3D Axes with `set_visible(False)` is skipped when drawing.

The fix is in `Figure.__getstate__`. It discards any dpi change caused by the device pixel ratio by setting `state["_dpi"] = state.get('_original_dpi', state['_dpi'])`. The pickled figure then keeps its original dpi, so it is no longer doubled on unpickling. I read this in the code but did not run it.

The bug is fixed in `Poly3DCollection.get_facecolor` in `art3d.py`. `_facecolors2d` is only set in `do_3d_projection`, so calling `get_facecolor()` before a draw raised the AttributeError. The fix checks `hasattr(self, '_facecolors2d')`. If the attribute is missing, it sets `self.axes.M = self.axes.get_proj()` and calls `self.do_3d_projection()` before returning `np.asarray(self._facecolors2d)`. The `hasattr` check is on line 1063. I didn't run the example. The ranked results also include a smoke test, `test_Poly3DCollection_get_facecolor`, which runs your example.

The error is raised in `Line3D.draw`, which unpacks `self._verts3d` (`xs3d, ys3d, zs3d = self._verts3d`). `_verts3d` is only assigned in `set_3d_properties` (line 222) and `set_data_3d` (line 247). The array-input failure from the first run ('input operand has more dimensions than allowed by the axis remapping') most likely stops `set_3d_properties` before it assigns `_verts3d`. The half-built Line3D stays on the axes, so every later draw hits the AttributeError. I did not run the reproduction to confirm this.

The feature is already implemented. Legend.__init__ in matplotlib/lib/matplotlib/legend.py takes a `draggable` keyword (default False). At the end of `__init__` it calls `self.set_draggable(state=draggable)`. PR #23913, "Add draggable as param to Legend init", added it in 3.7.0 and closed issue #9181, "legend draggable as keyword".

The bug is already fixed in this checkout. In `draw_text` in `backend_ps.py`, the glyph stream is no longer built with a `curr_stream` variable that could stay `None` for an empty line. It is now a plain list, `stream = []`. The loop at line 651 uses `itertools.groupby(stream, lambda entry: entry[0])`, so an empty line gives an empty stream and the loop body never runs. That removes the "cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType" error. I did not run the reproduction script.

The warning came from `Figure.__init__` treating any non-None `constrained_layout` value, including `False`, as a request for constrained layout. That installed a `ConstrainedLayoutEngine`, which isn't `adjust_compatible`. `subplots_adjust` then warned (figure.py:1343-1348) and returned without adjusting.

The code at figure.py:2499-2504 already has the fix. It only sets the constrained layout engine when `constrained_layout` is a dict (line 2501) or truthy (line 2503-2504), so `constrained_layout=False` no longer installs one. I read the code but didn't run the reproduction.

The StopIteration comes from `_safe_first_finite` in `matplotlib/lib/matplotlib/cbook.py`. It calls `next(...)` on a generator of finite values. When every value is nan, the generator is empty and `next` raises `StopIteration`. `Axes._convert_dx` calls it on `x0`, so `ax.bar([np.nan], [np.nan])` fails. In this checkout the line already has a fallback, `safe_first_element(obj)`, so it no longer raises for all-nan input.

The KeyError is expected behaviour, not a regression in `style.library`. In 3.6.0 the built-in seaborn style files were renamed with a `v0_8` prefix, so "seaborn-colorblind" became "seaborn-v0_8-colorblind". Use `plt.style.library["seaborn-v0_8-colorblind"]` instead. Matplotlib 3.6.2 (PR #24265) restored the old names in `style.library` with a deprecation warning. That shim has since been removed, and the current code in `lib/matplotlib/style/core.py` has no seaborn handling. The seaborn styles had drifted out of sync with seaborn itself since seaborn 0.9, so for current styles use seaborn directly.

Axis.set_ticks in lib/matplotlib/axis.py now raises ValueError('labels argument cannot be None when kwargs are passed') if kwargs are given without labels. This is the fix for the issue's "make any kwargs an error if labels is not set" option. I read the code but did not run it.

In Colormap.__call__, xa keeps the input dtype (uint8), so assigning the out-of-range indices _i_over/_i_under/_i_bad (256–258) into it triggers the NumPy 1.24 deprecation warning. The fix is to cast xa to int (`xa = xa.astype(int)`) before those assignments, which also covers unsigned ints.

The bug comes from `Normalize.autoscale`. In 3.6.3 it set `vmin = vmax = None` with callbacks live. The first assignment fired `changed`, which called the colorbar's `update_normal`. `_process_values` then saw an unscaled norm and set `norm.vmin = 0` and `norm.vmax = 1`. On a `LogNorm` that is invalid, so drawing raised "Invalid vmin or vmax". In this checkout, `autoscale` wraps the update in `with self.callbacks.blocked():` and sends a single `_changed()` at the end, so the colorbar never sees the half-reset norm. I read the code and did not run the reproduction.

The pickling failure came from DraggableBase storing the figure's canvas as an instance attribute. The fix makes `canvas` a property that looks it up through `ref_artist.figure.canvas`, so the unpicklable canvas is no longer part of the pickled state. The callbacks are also registered with `_connect_picklable`.

The fix is in `cbook.Grouper`, which `Figure.align_labels()` fills through `figure._align_label_groups`. It now defines `__getstate__` and `__setstate__`. `__getstate__` converts the `WeakKeyDictionary` of `WeakSet`s into plain dicts and sets, so pickle never sees a `weakref`. `__setstate__` rebuilds the weak references on load. I didn't run the reproduction script. The match is the pickle test at test_pickle.py:96, which calls `align_ylabels()` to cover these Groupers.

I did not reproduce this, and the cause is my best inference. It points at RangeSlider._update in lib/matplotlib/widgets.py. On a press inside the axes it sets drag_active and calls grab_mouse(self.ax) (line 874). It then goes on to update the value, which fires the on_changed callback. That callback calls clf(), and clf() releases the mouse grab through delaxes. I could not trace where input ends up blocked after that, so this is a hypothesis. The plain Slider._update (lines 534-536) has the same grab pattern. The Button path never grabs the mouse, which would explain why it works.

The crash comes from `DraggableBase.canvas`, a property that returns `self.ref_artist.figure.canvas`. When the annotation is removed, `ref_artist.figure` becomes None. `_check_still_parented` then calls `disconnect()`, and in the traceback's 3.7.1 code that goes through `self.canvas.mpl_disconnect(cid)`. That access raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'canvas'`.

In this checkout `disconnect()` already uses `_disconnectors` instead of `self.canvas`. I didn't run the reproduction, so I haven't confirmed the fix works.

Call `cb.update_normal(plot)` after setting `plot.norm = LogNorm()`. `Colorbar.update_normal` (colorbar.py:484) copies the mappable's cmap and norm onto the colorbar. If the norm differs, it resets the locator, formatter and scale, then redraws with `_draw_all()`. `update_bruteforce` is deprecated in favour of it. The reset step is at colorbar.py:501-503 (`if mappable.norm != self.norm: self.norm = mappable.norm; self._reset_locator_formatter_scale()`). I didn't run your example.

The no-effect behaviour you saw in your example comes from an older matplotlib. This code handles the norm change.

Two caveats from the docstring. A norm change resets any customized locator or formatter, so you would need to customize them again. A change to only *vmin*, *vmax* or *cmap* keeps the old ones.

Your `LogNorm()` has no vmin/vmax set yet, so you may also want to autoscale it. For example, call `plot.autoscale()` before `update_normal`.

The sibling axes are updated with emit=False in Axis._set_lim (axis.py), and the "xlim_changed"/"ylim_changed" callbacks are only processed inside `if emit:`, so shared axes never fire their callbacks.

The error comes from `_tick_only`, which does `ax.axis["bottom"].toggle(...)` and `ax.axis["left"].toggle(...)`. That only works for `mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1.mpl_axes.Axes`, where `axis` is a subscriptable dict-like object. On other axes classes such as `GeoAxes`, `axis` is a plain method, so the subscript raises `TypeError: 'method' object is not subscriptable`.

The bug is fixed in this code. For modules, `generate_autosummary_content` builds the template's `members` variable with `ModuleScanner.scan(imported_members)` instead of listing every attribute. `scan` marks a member as imported when it is a module, or when its `__module__` differs from the module's name. It drops imported members unless `autosummary_imported_members` is True, or the module defines `__all__` and `autosummary_ignore_module_all` is False. I only read the code and did not run the reproduction.

The backslash comes from `_escape_args_and_kwargs` in napoleon's docstring.py. When a name ends with `_` and the `strip_signature_backslash` config is set, it rewrites the trailing `_` as `\_`. The attributes section appears to go through this same escaping, so `hello_` renders as `hello\_`. I found this by reading the code. I did not run the reproduction or trace the attributes-section call path.

The index sort key in keyfunc (indexentries.py) decides which entries sort before or after the letters (letters and '_' go to group 1, everything else to group 0), while keyfunc3 separately assigns the 'Symbols' heading to every non-alpha, non-'_' first character. Because these two rules can disagree, groupby yields two separate 'Symbols' groups with the same name and anchor. The split happens at the sort-key check on line 103.

Implemented via the `man_make_section_directory` config option: when true, the man builder creates `man<section>` directories (e.g. man1) in the output dir and writes each page into its section directory.

FunctionDocumenter.format_signature now only uses the overload signatures when `autodoc_typehints != 'none'`. With 'none', it falls back to the normal `super().format_signature(**kwargs)` path. That path obeys the typehints setting. The fix is the `self.config.autodoc_typehints != 'none'` condition. I didn't check whether the method and `__init__`/`__new__` overload paths (around lines 1611 and 2219) have the same condition.

The fix is already in this codebase. The variable and attribute documenters pass `self.config.autodoc_type_aliases` to `get_type_hints()`, so the aliases apply. The module-level variable case (`DataDocumenter.add_directive_header`) does it at the cited line. The class attribute case (`AttributeDocumenter.add_directive_header`) does the same at `sphinx/sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py:2604`. The uninitialized-variable mixins also pass it, at lines 1950 and 2474. I read this in the code and did not build the example from the report.

The numref warning is emitted in StandardDomain._resolve_numref_xref (sphinx/domains/std.py) when get_fignumber raises ValueError (no entry in env.toc_fignumbers for the table/figure, e.g. target in a document not in the toctree / orphaned). In this checkout the message reads "Failed to create a cross reference. Any number is not assigned: %s".

The "Malformed option description" warning comes from the option:: directive handling in sphinx/domains/std.py. It is raised when option_desc_re (line 33) fails to match the option text. The regex is `((?:/|--|-|\+)?[^\s=]+)(=?\s*.*)`. It accepts any non-space, non-"=" characters as the option name, so `[enable=]PATTERN` parses as name `[enable` and args `=]PATTERN`. That matches test_cmd_option_starting_with_bracket in tests/test_domain_std.py. I did not run the tests.

In `ModuleDocumenter.get_object_members` (sphinx/ext/autodoc/__init__.py), the check is `if self.__all__ is None:`, so an empty `__all__` counts as set. Every member not listed in `__all__` is marked `skipped`, which means an empty `__all__` yields no members. The old behaviour came from a truthiness check (`if not self.__all__`) at this spot, which treated `[]` like a missing `__all__`. I did not run the repro. I only read the code, and this checkout already has the fix.

On Python before 3.9, `struct.Struct.__module__` is `_struct`, so Sphinx built the reference target as `_struct.Struct` and it couldn't be found. `INVALID_BUILTIN_CLASSES` in `sphinx/util/typing.py` maps `Struct` to `'struct.Struct'` (and `TracebackType` to `'types.TracebackType'`). `restify` and `stringify` use that mapping instead of the class's own module name. I read the mapping but didn't run the reproduction.

`_parse_other_parameters_section` in `sphinx/ext/napoleon/docstring.py` now checks `napoleon_use_param`. If it is set, the method renders the fields with `_format_docutils_params`. Otherwise it uses `_format_fields`. I took this from the ranked results and did not open the file to check the line number.

The epub check lives in `is_supported_builder` in `sphinx/sphinx/ext/viewcode.py`. It returns False for any builder whose name starts with `epub` when `viewcode_enable_epub` is False. `collect_pages` (line 228) calls it before generating module pages, and `ViewcodeAnchorTransform.run` (line 173) calls it to decide whether to keep the `[source]` links.

I read this code but did not run `make html epub`, so I haven't reproduced the bug. In this checkout the epub case already looks handled in `collect_pages`. `doctree_read` (line 69) has no such check, so it still collects module data for every builder, epub included. If the bug is still there, the likely cause is `_viewcode_modules` being shared across builders in a combined run. I didn't confirm that.

In `get_class_members` in sphinx/ext/autodoc/importer.py, annotation-only members found while walking the MRO get their docstring from `analyzer.attr_docs` (the `#:` comment). This is what stops them from being treated as undocumented. I read this from the code and did not run the reproduction.

The `:inherited-members:` option already accepts several classes in this code. `inherited_members_option` parses a comma-separated list of class names into a set, for example `:inherited-members: list,set,tuple`. `is_filtered_inherited_member` in `Documenter.filter_members` (line 651) then skips a member when it comes from a base class in that set (check at line 656). The docs in `autodoc.rst` describe the option but only show a single class. I didn't run it.

The bug is in `modify_field_list` in `sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py`. When `*name` or `**name` is already in `arguments`, the code only calls `arguments.get(name)` and discards the result (lines 123 and 126). It never assigns `arg` in those two branches, so `arg` is unbound or holds a stale value from an earlier loop iteration. The `'param'` and `'type'` checks then give wrong results. That is why `*args` and `**kwargs` get duplicated `param`/`type` fields. The fix is to assign `arg = arguments.get(name, {})` after the name is prefixed. I did not run a fix or the tests.

The bug is in `prepend_prolog` in `sphinx/sphinx/util/rst.py`. It uses `docinfo_re = re.compile(':\\w+:.*?')` (line 28) to find docinfo fields at the top of a document. A heading like ":mod:`mypackage2`" matches that pattern, so the heading line is treated as docinfo. The loop at line 83 counts it, and the prolog is inserted after the heading line instead of before it. That separates the heading from its underline, so the title is no longer recognised and drops out of the toctree. I haven't run the reproduction or tested a fix.

The fix is in `RequestHooksMixin.register_hook()`. It appends a callable hook, and if the value is iterable it extends the event's hook list with each callable in it. `Request.__init__` (models.py:221) and `prepare_hooks` both go through it, so lists in the hooks dict values are now accepted. I didn't run anything to confirm this.

In `Session.resolve_redirects`, each loop iteration starts with `prepared_request = req.copy()`. `req` is the original request, so a method changed by an earlier redirect (e.g. POST to GET on a 303) is lost. A later 307 then reissues the POST.

A raw socket.error raised while reading the response body is caught in urllib3's `HTTPResponse._error_catcher` and re-raised as `ProtocolError('Connection broken: ...')`. In `requests/models.py`, `iter_content.generate()` catches `ProtocolError` and re-raises it as `ChunkedEncodingError` (line 670-671). A `ReadTimeoutError` is re-raised as `ConnectionError` at line 674-675.

The `method = builtin_str(method)` line is no longer in `requests/sessions.py`. `Session.request` now calls `method.upper()` at line 452 and no longer converts the method with `builtin_str`. The conversion happens in `requests/models.py:324`, which uses `to_native_string(self.method.upper())`. That turns `b'GET'` into `'GET'` on Python 3 instead of `"b'GET'"`.

Requests already wraps urllib3's DecodeError. In `iter_content`'s `generate()` in `models.py`, `except DecodeError as e: raise ContentDecodingError(e)` converts it. In the same place, `ReadTimeoutError` becomes `ConnectionError` and `ProtocolError` becomes `ChunkedEncodingError`. HISTORY.rst notes that `ContentDecodingError` is "Raised instead of urllib3 DecodeError exceptions." I only checked `models.py`. I did not look at `adapters.py`, so I can't say whether the proxy-timeout `TimeoutError` is wrapped there.

iter_content(decode_unicode=True) returns bytes here because stream_decode_response_unicode passes chunks through undecoded when r.encoding is None. For application/json, requests doesn't set an encoding from the headers, since get_encoding_from_headers only defaults to ISO-8859-1 for text/* types. r.text still returns unicode because it falls back to apparent_encoding (chardet). iter_content doesn't use that fallback. To get unicode, set r.encoding (for example to 'utf-8') before iterating.
Blueprint.__init__ raises ValueError("'name' may not contain a dot '.' character.") when the blueprint name contains a dot.

Config.from_file() in flask/src/flask/config.py already has the mode option. It is a `text: bool = True` parameter, not `mode="b"`. `text=False` opens the file with "rb", so `app.config.from_file("config.toml", tomllib.load, text=False)` works. The parameter was added in Flask 2.3.

The `flask routes` command is `routes_command` in flask/src/flask/cli.py. It builds its table from `current_app.url_map.iter_rules()`. It prints only the headers ("Endpoint", "Methods", "Rule"), so it has no Domain column and ignores each rule's subdomain. To add the domain/subdomain, you would extend this function to include `rule.subdomain`.

Without changing Flask, you can get the same information yourself. Loop over `app.url_map.iter_rules()` and read `rule.subdomain`, `rule.endpoint`, `rule.methods` and `rule.rule` for each rule.
